sections.overview: Lethrinus laticaudis Alleyne & Macleay, 1877 is a western Pacific emperor, recorded from southern Indonesia and northern Australia to Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands.
sections.identification: It has a tan, brown or yellow body with irregular dark blotches; blue dots and short blue lines often mark the cheeks and head. It reaches about 56 cm total length.
sections.habitat: Juveniles use seagrass beds and mangrove swamps, while adults are found mainly over coral reefs.
sections.diet: Its diet consists mainly of crustaceans and fishes.
sections.behavior: It is often observed in schools, according to the FAO account.
sections.reproduction: The species accounts consulted do not provide a spawning calendar specific to L. laticaudis.
sections.ecology: Like Lethrinus microdon, it is an Indo-Pacific emperor, but their reported habitats differ: juvenile grass emperors use seagrass and mangroves, whereas smalltooth emperors are reported over sand near reefs.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists a 2015 IUCN assessment of Least Concern.
